**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Typical Value / Description |
|----------|----------|-----------------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| | State at STP | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (1 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14 K) |
| | Density (gas, STP) | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume (gas, STP) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | 0.754 eV |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Second ionization energy | 27.211 eV |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard entropy | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat capacity (gas, 298 K) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Speed of sound in H₂ | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (at 300 K) |
| | Refractive index (air) | ~1.00028 |
| | Viscosity (gas, 300 K) | 8.76 × 10⁻⁶ Pa s |
| | Thermal conductivity (gas, 300 K) | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Boiling point of H₂ (liquid) | 20.28 K |
| | Critical temperature | 33.41 K |
| | Critical pressure | 1.3 MPa |
| | Critical density | 0.313 g cm⁻³ |
| | Dipole moment | 0 (non‑polar) |
| | Bond length (H₂) | 0.741 Å |
| | Vibrational frequency (H₂) | 4401 cm⁻¹ |
| | Rotational constant (H₂) | 60.853 cm⁻¹ |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series (hydrogen atom); rotational/vibrational bands (H₂) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µ_N (proton) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Half‑life (tritium) | 12.32 years |
| | Radioactivity | Tritium emits β⁻ particles (max 18.6 keV) |
| | Solubility in water | ~1.6 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ at 25 °C |
| | Solubility in ethanol | ~0.001 mol L⁻¹ at 25 °C |
| | Solubility in liquid metals | Very high (e.g., ~0.5 mol kg⁻¹ in iron at 1000 °C) |
| | Reactivity | Extremely reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many organics |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Oxidation state | +1 (in most compounds) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| | Role in biology | Essential for energy metabolism (ATP synthesis), signaling (NO, H₂S), and as a building block in amino acids. |
| | Role in industry | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), feedstock for ammonia (Haber–Bosch), methanol, and various petrochemicals; used in semiconductor manufacturing (etching, doping). |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (water vapor only); storage and transport challenges (low density, high diffusivity). |
| | Safety | Highly flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % (v/v) in air; requires careful handling and ventilation. |
| | Isotopic applications | Deuterium used in nuclear fusion research (D–T fusion), neutron sources; tritium used in radiolabeling and fusion experiments. |
| | Spectroscopic significance | Hydrogen lines are the basis for the Balmer series, used in stellar classification and redshift measurements. |
| | Quantum mechanical significance | Hydrogen atom is the prototypical system for solving the Schrödinger equation; its energy levels are exactly solvable. |

---

### Quick Reference Highlights

- **Atomic number**: 1 → only one proton in the nucleus.
- **Isotopes**: ¹H (stable), ²H (stable, deuterium), ³H (radioactive, tritium).
- **Bonding**: H₂ is a diatomic molecule with a single covalent bond; H₂O, H₂SO₄, etc., show hydrogen’s ability to form polar covalent bonds.
- **Reactivity**: Forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂) and reacts with acids to release H₂ gas.
- **Energy**: Combustion of H₂ releases ~286 kJ mol⁻¹; used in fuel cells to produce electricity with only water as by‑product.
- **Physical state**: Gas at room temperature; liquid only below 20 K; solid below 14 K.
- **Spectroscopy**: Hydrogen’s spectral lines (Lyman, Balmer, Paschen) are fundamental to astrophysics and quantum mechanics.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
